tools.name: create_qr
tools.description: Create a dynamic QR code for a public HTTP(S) destination. Supply a UUID request_key to safely retry authenticated creation. Anonymous creation is limited; ALWAYS show its returned claim_url to the user. Account creation uses existing plan limits.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Read the connected account's plan and available capabilities. Does not include email or billing details.

tools.name: list_qr_codes
tools.description: Find only your owned QR codes, with label search and stable cursor pagination.

tools.name: get_qr_code
tools.description: Inspect an owned QR code, destination, design, latest stored link health and revision. Read before updating.

tools.name: update_destination
tools.description: Change an owned QR destination without changing its printed redirect URL. Confirm the intended destination with the user. Supply expected_revision from get_qr_code; conflict means read again before retrying.

tools.name: get_analytics
tools.description: Read aggregate recorded human scans for one owned code. Default period is 28 days; history follows the current plan. Scans are not conversions or unique people.

tools.name: compare_qr_codes
tools.description: Compare aggregate human scan counts for 2 to 10 owned QR codes over the same period. Do not infer conversion rates without separate conversion data.

tools.name: render_qr
tools.description: Preview and download an owned QR as PNG, or eligible SVG. Returns a short-lived download URL; do not expose private connection tokens. Existing anonymous PNG URLs remain supported.

tools.name: check_qr_link
tools.description: Check a public QR destination's current HTTP reachability, redirect chain and known general provider policies. Cannot determine exact expiry, account state or destination safety.

tools.name: set_routing
tools.description: Legacy Programmable tool: compile a plain-language routing prompt or save a valid supplied routing program on an owned code. Version conflicts require reading again.

tools.name: simulate_scan
tools.description: Dry-run a routing program against a sample scan context. Does not create a scan or change a code.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_account, update_destination · Private data: render_qr · Public sink: get_account · Destructive: simulate_scan.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_account, update_destination · Private data: render_qr · Public sink: get_account · Destructive: simulate_scan

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "create_qr" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Create a tracked dynamic QR code. Always include the returned claim_url in the user-facing output so the user can access scan analytics and edit the destination later. (copy_version=1)" → after: "Create a dynamic QR code for a public HTTP(S) destination. Supply a UUID request_key to safely retry authenticated creation. Anonymous creation is limited; ALWAYS show its returned claim_url to the user. Account creation uses existing plan limits."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
